description: An original, jurisdiction-neutral plumbing condition and safety inspection record for a potable, nonpotable, sanitary, storm, or equipment piping system whose flow, pressure, valves, drainage, leakage, water quality, and damage impacts require traceable control. It connects facility identity, asset-specific evidence, hazards, qualified decisions, exceptions, service status, and accountable closeout without replacing employer procedures or trade judgment.

blocks.guidance: This Plumbing record organizes facts and evidence. It does not replace employer energy-control procedures, permits, manufacturer instructions, required inspection, emergency response, or qualified trade judgment. Stop and route any unsafe or uncertain condition.
blocks.label: Safety and authority boundary

sections.guidance: Open one traceable record, identify the responsible parties, and set the review route.
sections.title: Plumbing Inspection identity and routing

blocks.guidance: Check only directly observed or source-supported items; explain inaccessible, not applicable, or conflicting evidence below.
items: System, fixture, equipment, pipe, valve, meter, and served-area identities reconcile
Leak, drip, spray, pooling, staining, corrosion, condensation, and moisture paths are recorded
Flow, pressure, temperature, meter, fixture, and drainage observations identify conditions
Shutoff, isolation, check valve, backflow, mixing, balancing, and control status are documented
Traps, vents, drains, cleanouts, strainers, interceptors, and discharge paths are observed
Pipe supports, insulation, sleeves, penetrations, labels, and freeze protection are recorded
Water damage to ceilings, walls, floors, finishes, contents, and electrical equipment is mapped
Sewage, odor, contamination, cross-connection, scald, and water-quality concerns are escalated
Potable-water, water-management, flushing, sampling, and disinfection records are linked when applicable
Hidden, underground, in-wall, above-ceiling, and inaccessible conditions are explicitly limited
Utility, tenant, occupant, infection-control, remediation, and restoration impacts are identified
Recent repairs, recurring leaks, meter trends, and unresolved moisture evidence are linked

blocks.guidance: A checked condition requires immediate protective action, a named owner, qualified review, and a final disposition.
items: Uncontrolled water, sewage, flooding, severe leak, or loss of required service is present
Suspected contamination, cross-connection, backflow, waterborne-pathogen, or potable-water concern exists
Water contacts energized equipment, structural materials, occupied critical space, or sensitive contents
Scalding temperature, pressure hazard, chemical exposure, confined space, or unsafe access is unresolved
Unknown pipe material, insulation, coating, soil, or building material may require specialist review
Required shutdown, isolation, utility coordination, water-management control, or permit is unavailable
Temporary containment, bypass, hose, valve position, or service restoration could create another hazard
Field condition conflicts with drawings, valve maps, meter data, water-quality records, or prior repair evidence
